label: Last Glacial Maximum
note: Ice sheets at their largest; northern ice began retreating 20,000–19,000 years ago and sea level rose.

label: Holocene begins
note: Formal start of the current warm epoch, dated by counting annual layers in a Greenland ice core.

label: Farming begins, Fertile Crescent
note: Plants and animals domesticated in the Near East during the warm, stable early Holocene.

label: 8.2-kiloyear cold event
note: A short, sharp cooling that marks the start of the middle Holocene.

label: Mid-Holocene
note: Some reconstructions show a warm peak here, others steady warming: the records disagree.

label: 4.2-kiloyear event
note: Drought and cooling that marks the start of the latest Holocene stage.

label: Little Ice Age
note: Cold in many regions, but not everywhere at the same time: no globally synchronous cold period.

label: Watt's steam engine
note: The separate condenser made steam engines efficient enough to power factories: the Industrial Revolution gathers pace.

label: Tambora erupts
note: The largest eruption in recorded history; its haze caused 1816's 'year without a summer'.

label: Fourier: the atmosphere keeps Earth warm
note: Joseph Fourier argues that the atmosphere keeps Earth warmer than it would otherwise be: an idea later called the greenhouse effect.

label: Thermometer record begins
note: 1850–1900 is the reference used to measure warming since pre-industrial times.

label: Foote: CO₂ warms in sunlight
note: Eunice Foote finds air with CO₂ heats most in sunlight and suggests more CO₂ would warm the Earth.

label: Tyndall measures heat-trapping gases
note: Lab experiments show water vapour and CO₂ absorb heat radiation.

label: Krakatau erupts
note: Its aerosols lowered global temperatures by up to 0.5 °C the following year; they returned to normal by 1888.

label: Arrhenius calculates CO₂ warming
note: The first calculation of how much more CO₂ would warm the Earth.

label: First powered flight
note: The Wright brothers fly 12 seconds at Kitty Hawk.

label: Callendar links warming to fuel
note: Shows that burning fossil fuels has already raised CO₂ and temperatures.

label: Great Acceleration
note: After 1950 energy use, population, economies and emissions all rise steeply.

label: Revelle & Suess: oceans won't absorb it all
note: Much of the CO₂ from fuel will stay in the air.

label: CO₂ measurements at Mauna Loa begin
note: Charles Keeling's record starts at 313 ppm.

label: Teller warns oil industry about CO₂
note: At an oil-industry centenary symposium, physicist Edward Teller warns that fuel CO₂ could warm the climate.

label: US science advisers warn of CO₂
note: A report to President Johnson projects CO₂ about 25% higher by 2000 and warns of climate change.

label: First realistic climate model
note: Manabe and Wetherald calculate warming from doubled CO₂.

label: Report for oil industry warns of warming
note: A Stanford Research Institute report for the American Petroleum Institute says rising CO₂ would likely cause significant warming by 2000.

label: Moon landing
note: Apollo 11: the first people on the Moon.

label: Total's magazine explains CO₂ warming
note: An article in Total's in-house magazine, by an outside geographer, explains warming from rising CO₂.

label: Oil crisis
note: The Arab oil embargo; emissions dip (computed from our data).

label: Exxon's projections matched reality
note: A 2023 study finds 63–83% of Exxon scientists' warming projections were accurate.

label: Exxon scientist briefs top management
note: Exxon scientist James Black tells the management committee that CO₂ from fossil fuels is the most likely way humans are influencing the climate; doubling it could warm the globe by 1–3 °C.

label: Charney report
note: US scientists put warming from doubled CO₂ at about 3 °C, give or take 1.5 °C.

label: Oil industry CO₂ task force briefed
note: A consultant tells the American Petroleum Institute's CO₂ and Climate Task Force, with members from Exxon, Texaco and Sohio, to expect about 2.5 °C of global warming by 2038.

label: Exxon's internal CO₂ primer
note: An internal Exxon review estimates that doubling CO₂ could raise global temperature by about 1.3–3.1 °C.

label: Montreal Protocol
note: Phased out ozone-destroying gases, many of them strong greenhouse gases too.

label: IPCC founded
note: Set up by WMO and UNEP to assess climate science for governments.

label: Hansen tells US Senate warming is detected
note: 'The greenhouse effect has been detected, and it is changing our climate now.'

label: Shell's confidential greenhouse report
note: Notes that fuels sold by the Shell Group made up about 4% of global CO₂ emissions from burning fuels in 1984, and warns of large climate changes.

label: Berlin Wall falls
note: The end of the Cold War; the Soviet Union dissolves two years later.

label: Soviet Union collapses
note: Russia's fossil CO₂ fell 42% from 1990 to 1998; world emissions dipped only briefly (computed from our data).

label: Pinatubo erupts
note: About 20 million tonnes of sulphur dioxide reached the stratosphere; Earth's surface cooled for about three years, by up to about 0.7 °C (1.3 °F).

label: UN climate convention
note: Adopted in May 1992 and signed at the Rio Earth Summit; in force since 1994.

label: Kyoto Protocol
note: The first treaty with binding emission targets for industrialised countries.

label: Paris Agreement
note: Countries agree to hold warming well below 2 °C and pursue 1.5 °C.

label: COVID-19 pandemic
note: Fossil CO₂ emissions fell about 5% in one year, the largest drop on record, then rebounded.

label: First year above 1.5 °C
note: The first calendar year more than 1.5 °C above 1850–1900; the Paris limit refers to long-term averages.
